name: Synvera
description: Synvera is a cross-modal neuromodulator that deliberately disrupts the thalamic relay's sensory sorting function, causing signals from one sense to bleed into the processing centers of another. Users taste sound as distinct flavors — bass as something rich and bitter, high frequencies as sharp and citrus — while color produces audible tones and touch generates visual impressions. Nightshade sells it legally as a 'perceptual research compound' while the recreational market is openly its primary consumer.
effects: full synesthetic cross-modal fusion across all five senses
music becomes a full gustatory-visual-tactile experience
side_effects: nausea if synesthetic input conflicts (e.g., loud, harsh sounds experienced as foul taste)
sensory confusion persisting 1-2 hours after primary effect
chronic use degrades thalamic sorting — partial synesthesia becomes permanent
cultural_context: Synvera is the drug of Shelf artists, street musicians, and anyone who wants to experience beauty without the money to buy it. On the Shelf, a single cartridge shared among four people at a fire-lit gathering is a ritual — people describe Synvera nights as the most beautiful experiences of their lives. Nightshade's legal fiction fools no one but the law moves slowly. Permanent synesthesia from chronic use is common enough on the Shelf that some communities have built entire social languages around it.
story_hooks: A Shelf musician has been using Synvera for six years and now has permanent full synesthesia — she can't turn it off, and it's destroying her ability to sleep, but her music is being discovered by Tier 4 collectors

Nightshade is quietly reformulating Synvera to make the permanent synesthesia side effect more likely — they're researching whether permanently altered users become dependent on Synvera to manage the permanent condition
A Tier 3 neuroscientist believes Synvera-induced synesthesia is producing genuine new cognitive architectures and wants to study Shelf communities — but needs a fixer to gain access
